newsitem.title: USA: Floppy disk market grew 10 pct in 1996 - Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: Floppy disk market grew 10 pct in 1996 - Dataquest.

text.p: Global shipments of flexible, or floppy, disk drives grew by 10.3 percent to 89.6 million units in 1996, despite the fact that many computers are now equipped with CD-ROM and high-capactiy "Zip" drives, Dataquest said.
But prices for floppy drives fell by 9.7 percent, the market research firm said.

Mitsumi Electric Co Ltd had the largest market share with 19.1 percent up from 16.8 percent in 1995, while TEAC Corp dropped to the second position with 18.5 percent market share, off from 19.3 the previous year.
"Prices will continue to erode, even with fewer suppliers offering flexible disk drive products," said Phil Devin, chief analyst of Dataquest's Computer Storage program.
"Vendors will move to the more complex, high-capacity drives where the profits will support investment for the future," he added.
"Quick acceptance of the Zip or LS-120 drives by several of the top PC makers would swing the pendulum quickly away from 1.44MB drives."
